verdict: rigs.data.js clears the bar. All 15 acceptance criteria pass against the real file, verified by execution rather than reading: node --check passes, the export set is exactly the ten pinned names with the pinned arities and no extras, the six entries match the ratified table field-for-field (weights sum to 100, 60k-roll distribution lands on 40.0/25.9/18.2/10.0/4.9/1.0), effectiveRuns reproduces the three hand-checkable cases (8x0.30=2, 5x0.18 clamps to 1, 3x1.15=3), the perk mapping is a single clamped tier with no summation, and grep is clean for ironback, every Garage SKU id, _convoyCanSend, window/document/Profile/Corp/Forge outside comments, and the settled out-of-scope words. Its comments are the real work: the not-merged-into-PP_VEHICLE_NAMES decision is argued and costed against two named read sites, lotSlots is recorded as a rejected enforcement with the dozen sites that would have to move together, the condition table is declared a MIRROR with index.html named as authority and drift wired to a runnable alarm, the provisional pricing block pre-writes its own deletion, and the one legacy inconsistency it found (the auction win path assigning slot = p.lot.length while the other paths scan for the first free slot) is flagged as read from the code and explicitly unmeasured rather than dressed up as an incident. Spot-checked its factual claims against index.html and they hold. What keeps this from being flawless is that the file's own headline safety feature is vacuous in the only wiring that exists.
biggest_gap: auditRigs()'s drift alarm silently no-ops on a non-object condMult, and that is exactly how the only caller invokes it. rigs.data.js:510 gates the whole check on `if (condMult && typeof condMult === 'object')` with no else, while public/src/transport/index.js:826 passes an accessor FUNCTION — `(c) => num(call(b.condMult, 1, c))` — under a comment claiming it is 'Handed the LIVE ... condition multipliers off the bridge'. Executed: auditRigs(ids, driftedObject) reports the drift; auditRigs(ids, sameDriftAsFunction) returns []. The file's own header warns that a stale mirror 'makes the corresponding rule pass VACUOUSLY, which is the direction that hides bugs' and then ships a third instance of it. Fix inside this file: duck-type a function accessor the way rigById already duck-types id-or-entry, and when condMult is neither, push a problem string saying the drift check was skipped rather than returning clean.

The auction-slot inconsistency the file reports is real: index.html:196914 `const slot = (p && Array.isArray(p.lot)) ? p.lot.length : 0;` against the first-free scans at 196294 and 80471. Two smaller inaccuracies: the risk-unit comment quotes the paid table as '0.05, 0.12, 0.20' where rig_warden is 0.22, and the _opEcon block asserts 'Transport has no OPS_ECON entry' which the working tree has since falsified (index.html:79789 now carries `transport: { startup: 650000, ... }`), so the comment's own stated expiry has arrived.
